jobs.title: Compensation Program Manager
jobs.description:
**Remote**

Job Overview:

The Compensation Program Manager partners with HR, Finance, and business leaders in the design, administration, governance, and continuous improvement of enterprise compensation programs, including incentive compensation plans and annual merit planning. This role also manages compensation compliance, project management (PMO), communications and training.

Job Responsibilities:

-
Oversee the annual compensation planning cycles, including annual merit budget setting, cycle scheduling, stakeholder communications, manager and HR training, executive reporting, governance, approvals, audit controls, and overall program oversight.

-
Partner with Total Payroll Operations, Finance, IT, and HR teams in the setup, testing, administration, and continuous improvement of systems, workflows, and processes supporting monthly, quarterly, and annual compensation cycles.

-
Provide executive updates, analytics, and reporting related to merit planning outcomes, budget utilization, pay-for-performance results, and compensation program effectiveness.

-
Manage incentive compensation plans in partnership with Finance, Sales, and business leaders, to define plan metrics, measures, weightings, and governance.

-
Design, administer, and evaluate short-term incentive programs, including modeling, scenario analysis, and plan documentation, in partnership with the Sr. Compensation Analyst - Incentives.

-
Ensure that incentive compensation plans and results are effectively communicated to participants.

-
Develop and maintain dashboards and reporting tools to monitor plan performance and payouts.

-
Ensure the accuracy of incentive plan eligibility, calculations, approvals, accruals, and payments through strong controls, audits, and administration processes.

-
Help drive continuous improvement of compensation plan design, administration, communications, and governance to help maximize plan effectiveness.

-
Develop and deliver compensation training and education tools to support a consistent understanding and application of compensation programs.

-
Ensure compensation compliance with federal, state, and local requirements, including pay equity, minimum wage, minimum salary thresholds, pay transparency regulations, FLSA classification standards, Department of Labor requirements, and state/provincial reporting obligations.

-
Monitor compensation programs to ensure alignment with the company’s compensation philosophy of pay-for-results, pay equity, and market competitiveness.

-
Serve as PMO lead for enterprise compensation projects, coordinating timelines, resources, governance, stakeholders, risks, dependencies, and implementation activities.

-
Maintain and enhance the enterprise compensation calendar to capture and track key dates related to compensation cycles, communications, training, and projects.

-
Help shape and implement improvements in compensation training, manager enablement, and communication strategies to support effective decision-making. Help ensure effective change management strategies for HR, managers, and business leaders specific to compensation.

-
Maintain compensation workflows, documentation, governance standards, and audit controls.

-
Support benchmarking, market pricing, salary structures, and job architecture.

- Perform other duties as required.

Job Requirements:

Education/ Certifications:

- Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business, Finance, or related field; CCP or PHR is a plus.

Experience:

- 6–8 years of progressive compensation experience, with direct ownership of annual merit review cycles, incentive compensation design and administration, and compensation compliance programs.

-
Experience leading cross-functional projects and working with common HRIS systems and reporting tools (PeopleSoft, Workday, SAP or comparable HCM; PayScale/PayFactors or comparable survey/benchmarking tools)

Knowledge and Skills:

- Advanced analytical skills: ability to interpret large datasets and build compensation models.

- Deep knowledge of compensation regulations, pay equity analytics, FLSA classification standards, and market pricing methodologies.

- Proficiency with Excel, HRIS, reporting dashboards, and compensation planning tools.

- Strong written and verbal communication, presentation development (PowerPoint) and change management skills.

- Strong project management skills; Understanding of best practice PM methodologies (Lean, Agile, Waterfall, etc.) a plus.

- Ability to manage multiple complex programs simultaneously and work collaboratively across functions.

- Good judgment is required for this position as there may be times when direct supervision may not be immediately available. (Legal requirement to add in this language)

Work Environment:

Remote Role:

- This position is classified as remote where the associate will perform remote work from their primary residence. Remote associates are welcome to work from the office but are not required to do so. While remote associates are not required to work from an office on a regular basis, they may be required to come to the office or other UNFI locations for necessary business reasons or if directed to do so by their manager

Travel (minor):

- This position may require the associate to travel to company offices, distribution centers, or other locations for specific meetings or other business reasons.

Physical Environment/Demands:

Office Roles:

·Most work is performed in a temperature-controlled office environment.

·Incumbent may sit for long periods of time at a desk or computer terminal.

·While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; and talk or hear.

·Incumbent may use calculators, keyboards, telephones, and other office equipment in the course of a normal workday.

·Stooping, bending, twisting, and reaching may be required in the completion of job duties.

About UNFI: We are North America’s premier grocery wholesaler, delivering the widest variety of fresh, branded, and owned brand products to community grocers and retail chains alike. A pioneer in natural and organic foods, we are growing and transforming to meet the needs of an evolving workplace. Our 29,000+ employees work across America in our 50 Distribution Centers and corporate offices. Learn more: Organic, Natural and Conventional Food | Wholesale Food Distributors | UNFI

jobs.title: Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Join our team and immediately become part of the largest distributor of conventional, natural, organic and specialty products in the United States and Canada. We serve over 43,000 customer locations with 200,000 different products. Our Warehouse associates supply thousands of consumers with better for you food that nourishes families nationwide. Our retailers range from small family-owned stores to Wholefoods Markets and everything in between. Are you ready to make an impact on the lives of others and feel good about what you do? Join our growing Distribution team today.

- Competitive Benefits - Medical, Dental, Vision, 401K & Vacation

- Growth and professional development opportunities.

- Recognition for great work, company events and picnics, and much more.

- Full-time employment opportunity

Purpose:

Responsible for planning, organizing, and directing the shipping/receiving/facility related activities of the Warehouse. Responsible for enforcing productivity and quality rates, reviews/pay adjustments, E-Time (payroll), and any other related issues to ensure that the daily workload is completed efficiently and accurately. Responsible for keeping the shift staffed and disciplined at a level where the work will be completed in an efficient manner. Ensure Warehouse operations are in accordance with established procedures and policies. Keeps management well informed of significant problems and area activities.

What does it mean to be a part of our Warehouse Operations Manager team?

A Warehouse Operations Manager is responsible for overseeing and optimizing all aspects of warehouse functions to ensure efficient and cost-effective operations. This role involves managing the movement, storage, and distribution of goods, as well as supervising warehouse staff, implementing operational strategies, and ensuring compliance with company standards and regulations. This position plays a key role in driving improvements in warehouse productivity, safety, and customer satisfaction.  At UNFI, we strive to help make our customers stronger, our supply chain better, and our fresh food solutions more inspired.

Job Responsibilities:

-
Manages all day-to day activities surrounding inbound, outbound, inventory control, AND/OR facility warehouse operations.

-
Monitors, research, and implements solutions regarding issues related to damaged product, mis-shipped product, and missing product.

-
Assists in developing / adjusting of policies and procedures for warehouse operations.

-
Manages equipment needs and suggests investments for capital improvements.

-
Ensures that Warehouse materials are rotated and stored properly.

-
Assumes responsibility for the maintenance of Warehouse facilities. Ensures that both the inside and outside of the facilities are clean and orderly.

-
Works to develop and maintain productive business relations with internal and external customers.

- Provides leadership to direct reports while focusing on process improvements and creating a high-performance supervisory team.

- Manages labor needs to ensure business needs are met in an efficient manner.

- Fosters positive employee relations, while ensuring Company vision and mission are active.

- Manages performance of direct reports and also ensuring accountability at all levels within dept. Ensures operations meet or exceed Company metrics.

- Partners with Human Resources to find and retain talent.

- Ensures all company policies are followed and implements proper solutions when needed.

- Maintains or develops reports to understand the state of operations, or where to make improvements.

- Perform duties in accordance with Hazard Analysis Critical Control Points (HACCP) and Safe Quality Food (SQF) policies and procedures, as appropriate for location.

- Performs other duties as assigned.

Job Requirements:

Education/ Certifications: Required/Preferred list requirement is required or preferred)

- Additional related facility management training preferred

Experience:

- Five or more years of related experience, with at least two or more years of supervisory experience

- 3 – 5 years warehouse management and/or logistics management experience in a complex, service-driven organization

- Experience in shipping/receiving is preferred

- Good judgment is required for this position as there may be times when direct supervision may not be immediately available.

Knowledge:

- Must have strong knowledge of all warehouse procedures and functions

- Knowledge of budgeting, supply contracts, and shipping requirements

Skills/ Abilities:

- Excellent leadership abilities

- Keen eye for quality; detail oriented with excellent analytical skills

- Able to organize, coordinate, and direct team activities

- Strong problem-solving skills

- Ability to work in a team environment

- Must be flexible

- Ability to understand Accounting, HR and Payroll activities/practices

jobs.title: Liquor Operations Manager - Hybrid - Edina, MN
jobs.description:
*This is a hybrid role out of the Edina, MN office.

Job Overview:

The Liquor Operations Manager provides elevated field leadership and strategic operational oversight between the Liquor Merchandising team, store leadership, and liquor store locations to ensure consistent execution of buying, receiving, merchandising, inventory management, and operational standards. This role is accountable for improving operational excellence, reinforce merchandising strategies, improving inventory accuracy, shrink results, and delivering an exceptional customer experience across all liquor locations.

As a higher-level leadership role, the Liquor Operations Manager is expected to influence Store Directors, Department Managers, District Directors, Merchandising, and other cross-functional partners to deliver measurable business results. The role moves beyond support and monitoring by establishing clear expectations, diagnosing root causes, leading market-level action plans, developing leadership capability, and holding teams accountable for sustained improvement in sales, gross profit, shrink, labor productivity, inventory accuracy, and operational standards.

Job Responsibilities:

- Lead liquor operational execution across assigned stores or market, setting clear expectations for standards, priorities, accountability, and measurable performance outcomes.

- Conduct regular store visits and operational assessments to evaluate merchandising, cleanliness, in-stock conditions, inventory accuracy, pricing and signing, production execution, labor effectiveness, and compliance with company standards.

- Own the identification of performance gaps, root causes, and corrective actions; build sustainable store and market-level action plans that improve execution, accountability, and financial results.

- Accountable for liquor store financial performance by analyzing and delivering sales, gross profit, shrink, labor, productivity, inventory turns, ordering effectiveness, production planning, and department-level operating metrics across districts.

- Develop liquor store operational strategies and execution frameworks that improve long-term business performance.

- Partner with Merchandising, Finance, Supply Chain, and Store Operations leadership to shape future operating standards and business priorities.

- Provide operational guidance and recommendations that influence district leadership.

- Lead shrink reduction strategy and execution by identifying loss drivers, strengthening inventory controls, improving product rotation and handling practices, reinforcing production discipline, and ensuring stores are held accountable for results.

- Improve ordering discipline, forecast alignment, inventory levels, out-of-stock conditions, and overstock opportunities to support sales growth, customer satisfaction, and waste reduction.

- Advanced working knowledge of Minnesota liquor laws, regulations, and statutes

- May include THC

- Acts as a liaison and counterpart to the Category Merchants relationships with Distributor partners.

- Meets regularly (monthly) with Merchandising team to align initiatives and plans.

- Displays, merchandising, buying, quantity deals needed to meet ad forecasting metrics

- Coach Liquor Managers on disciplined buying practices, including promotional purchases, seasonal commitments, replenishment strategies, inventory levels, and opportunity buys that support sales, margin, and inventory objectives.

- Support receiving accuracy by reinforcing best practices for invoice reconciliation, product verification, shortage resolution, damage processing, and timely movement of merchandise to the sales floor.

- Provide data-driven recommendations and decision support to improve sales, profitability, labor effectiveness, shrink, in-stock position, and customer experience.

- Serve as a key field leader and connector between Store Operations, Merchandising, Category Management, Supply Chain, and other support partners to remove barriers and improve fresh performance.

- Support new store openings, remodels, resets, seasonal sets, and grand openings by coordinating merchandising execution, product readiness, fixture setup, receiving flow, signage, and operational readiness.

- Measure effectiveness of operational initiatives through store visits, performance scorecards, department results, follow-up evaluations, and continuous improvement routines.

- Translate field insights, customer trends, competitive activity, and operational results into recommendations that influence merchandising strategies, process improvements, and business priorities.

- Act as the subject matter expert for total liquor operations, providing leadership guidance, best practices, escalation support, and execution direction across assigned stores.

- Reinforce performance accountability through timely feedback, progress reviews, coaching conversations, follow-up routines, recognition of improvement, and escalation of unresolved execution gaps.

- Performs other duties as assigned.

Job Requirements: Education/ Certifications:

- Bachelor’s degree or four years of experience in a similar or related role.

Experience:

- Five or more years of progressive retail grocery leadership experience preferred or equivalent leadership experience.

- Demonstrated leadership experience across liquor stores with responsibility for execution and financial performance strongly preferred.

- Experience leading through others, influencing cross-functional partners, managing store or market-level performance, and driving measurable improvement in sales, shrink, labor, gross profit, and operational standards preferred.

- Experience influencing strategic business decisions.

Knowledge/Skills/ Abilities

- Advanced knowledge of total liquor operations, including merchandising standards, food safety, production planning, inventory management, ordering, labor utilization, shrink controls, and customer experience.

- Strong financial and analytical acumen with the ability to interpret sales, gross profit, shrink, labor, productivity, inventory, and customer metrics and translate results into clear priorities and action plans.

- Proven ability to diagnose root causes, prioritize opportunities, establish routines, and lead sustainable operational improvements across multiple stores or departments.

- Strong leadership, coaching, influencing, and relationship-building skills with the ability to develop Store Directors, Department Managers, and cross-functional partners without direct authority.

- Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and facilitation skills with the ability to communicate performance insights, priorities, and recommendations clearly to store, district, and senior operations leaders.

- Ability to manage multiple markets, stores, initiatives, and priorities while operating independently in a high-travel, field-based leadership environment.

- Sound judgment, decision-making, business ownership, and organizational skills with the ability to set direction, follow up consistently, and hold teams accountable for achieving company goals.

- Incumbent may use calculators, keyboards, telephones, and other office equipment in the course of a normal workday.

jobs.title: Fresh Operations Manager -Edina, MN
jobs.description:
This role is hybrid out of the Edina, MN location.

Job Overview:

The Fresh Operations Manager provides elevated field leadership and strategic operational oversight across all fresh perishable departments, including Meat, Seafood, Produce, Floral, Bakery, and Deli. This role is accountable for improving fresh department execution, financial performance, shrink results, merchandising consistency, food safety compliance, and customer experience across assigned stores or markets.

As a higher-level leadership role, the Fresh Operations Manager is expected to influence Store Directors, Department Managers, District Directors, Merchandising, and other cross-functional partners to deliver measurable business results. The role moves beyond support and monitoring by establishing clear expectations, diagnosing root causes, leading market-level action plans, developing leadership capability, and holding teams accountable for sustained improvement in sales, gross profit, shrink, labor productivity, inventory accuracy, freshness, and operational standards.

Job Responsibilities:

- Serve as the subject matter expert (SME) for six fresh departments – Meat, Seafood, Produce, Floral, Bakery, and Deli - demonstrating deep knowledge of department-specific operations, tools, processes, standards, merchandising, production, inventory management, labor practices, and financial drivers.

- Lead fresh operational execution across assigned stores or markets, by translating company standards, priorities, and business strategies into clear expectations, routines, measurable outcomes, and accountability across Meat, Seafood, Produce, Floral, Bakery, and Deli.

- Conduct regular store visits and operational assessments across the six fresh departments to evaluate merchandising, freshness, cleanliness, food safety, in-stock conditions, inventory accuracy, pricing and signing, production execution, labor effectiveness, and compliance with company standards.

- Own the identification of performance gaps, root causes, and develop sustainable corrective action plans that address both immediate execution issues and underlying capability gaps, driving measurable improvements in operational performance, accountability, and financial results.

- Own and influence fresh financial performance by analyzing and improving sales, gross profit, shrink, labor, productivity, inventory turns, ordering effectiveness, production planning, and other department-level operating metrics across districts.

- Develop fresh operational strategies and execution frameworks that improve long-term business performance.

- Develop and implement fresh operational strategies, standards, routines, and execution frameworks that strengthen consistency across the six departments and improve long-term business performance. Serve as a trusted operational resource to Store Directors and District leadership, providing hands-on expertise, recommendations, escalation support, and practical solutions that strengthen execution across all six fresh departments.

- Lead shrink reduction strategy and execution by identifying department-specific loss drivers, strengthening inventory controls, improving product rotation and handling practices, reinforcing production discipline, and building store leadership capability to sustain results.

- Improve ordering, forecasting, inventory, and production disciplines by leveraging department expertise and business data to optimize inventory levels, reduce out-of-stocks and overstock, improve freshness and waste, and support sales and customer satisfaction.

- Build fresh leadership capability across the organization by coaching Store Directors, Department Managers, and emerging leaders through practical application of department-specific knowledge, including production planning, labor utilization, shelf-life management, inventory control, ordering, merchandising, standards execution, and financial decision-making.

- Provide data-driven decision support and recommendations to district and store leadership to improve sales, profitability, labor effectiveness, shrink, in-stock position, freshness, and customer experience.

- Serve as a key field connector between Store Operations, Merchandising, Category Management, Supply Chain, Finance, and other support partners by translating field needs and department-specific requirements into actionable solutions and removing barriers to execution.

- Lead or support new store openings, remodels, department resets, leadership transitions, operational pilots, and implementation of new fresh programs, tools, processes, and technology, ensuring department-specific requirements are effectively executed.

- Measure and sustain the effectiveness of operational initiatives through store visits, performance scorecards, department results, follow-up evaluations, capability assessments, and continuous improvement routines.

- Translate field insights, customer trends, competitive activity, department expertise, and operational performance data into actionable recommendations that influence merchandising strategies, process improvements, operating standards, and business priorities.

- Reinforce performance accountability through timely feedback, coaching, progress reviews, recognition, and follow-up, escalating unresolved execution gaps and ensuring agreed-upon actions result in sustained improvement.

- Performs other duties as assigned.

- Bachelor’s degree or four years of experience in a similar or related role.

Experience:

- Five or more years of progressive retail grocery leadership experience preferred or equivalent leadership experience.

- Demonstrated leadership experience across fresh perishable departments, including Meat, Seafood, Produce, Floral, Bakery, or Deli, with responsibility for execution and financial performance strongly preferred.

- Experience leading through leaders, influencing cross-functional partners, managing store or market-level performance, and driving measurable improvement in sales, shrink, labor, gross profit, and operational standards preferred.

- Experience influencing strategic business decisions.
